title: Port Alder Rising
premise: Marine biologist Marguerite Eastwick has spent three years in Port Alder rebuilding herself after a scandal that cost her everything, finding safety in turtle counts, tide charts, and small careful steps. When the town's beloved anonymous pen-pal program pairs her with a stranger, the letters become the one place she is honest — until she discovers her correspondent is Callum Voss, the harbor developer whose marina project will destroy the turtle nesting grounds, and the man she has been publicly feuding with all season. As Marguerite works with Callum's estranged sister and a retired judge to expose the corrupt permit deal behind the marina, she realizes the letters were never anonymous to him at all, and that he has been protecting her name from the same powerful family that ruined her. When the truth of her past threatens to surface at a public hearing, Marguerite must choose between the safe career she rebuilt and the man who saw her clearly all along, choosing at last to testify, save the nesting grounds, and claim both justice and love on her own terms.
about_author: Bram Kavanagh is the pen name of a former fisheries observer who spent a decade on working boats along the Atlantic coast before turning to fiction. They write romances about people who rebuild themselves in small towns with long memories.

chapters.title: Counting Instead of Breathing
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Three years after a research scandal destroyed her career, she runs dawn turtle surveys in Port Alder, measuring her recovery in safe small steps. Emotional beat: fragile calm established, and the reader sees how carefully she has built walls.

chapters.title: The Town That Keeps Letters
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Port Alder's cherished anonymous pen-pal program opens its winter sign-ups; her landlady signs her up against her protests. Emotional beat: reluctant warmth, the town's insistence that no one heals alone.

chapters.title: A Man with a Dredge
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Developer Callum Voss arrives to push the Alder Point Marina project, cold, efficient, and privately haunted by the sister he left behind in this town. Emotional beat: guarded ambition masking old guilt.

chapters.title: First Collision
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. At a raucous town meeting, Marguerite publicly tears into Callum's marina plans, and he gives as good as he gets. Emotional beat: electric antagonism — two people who cannot stop looking at each other while fighting.

chapters.title: Dear Stranger
chapters.summary: Alternating letters. Marguerite and her anonymous pen pal exchange first letters; both are stiff, then unexpectedly honest. Emotional beat: the strange relief of telling the truth to no one.

chapters.title: Nesting Season Deadlines
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She maps the nesting beach that the marina's dredging schedule would destroy, and petitions the town council. Emotional beat: purpose rekindled — she is fighting for something again, not just surviving.

chapters.title: The Voss Name
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Callum's sister Nell refuses to speak to him; he signs up for the pen-pal program on a drunken dare, wanting one relationship without his name attached. Emotional beat: loneliness under armor.

chapters.title: What I Never Told Anyone
chapters.summary: Letters. Marguerite writes her pen pal about the scandal in fragments — a falsified dataset, a mentor who betrayed her, a career she fled. Emotional beat: confession without consequences.

chapters.title: Coffee, Hostile
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Forced onto a permit-review committee together, Marguerite and Callum argue over coffee and discover an unsettling ease in each other's company. Emotional beat: attraction disguised as irritation.

chapters.title: The Permit That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Reviewing files, Callum finds the marina's coastal permit was fast-tracked by the Hollis family — the town's old-money power — and that his own firm was chosen to be their shield. Emotional beat: first crack in his certainty.

chapters.title: Letters in the Dark
chapters.summary: Letters. The pen pals trade fears; Marguerite admits she is terrified of being seen, and her correspondent admits he is terrified of being known. Emotional beat: intimacy accelerating past either's defenses.

chapters.title: Storm on the Survey
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A squall strands Marguerite and Callum together on the survey boat; they shelter, argue, and he carries a stranded hatchling bucket through the rain without being asked. Emotional beat: the wall develops its first door.

chapters.title: Nell Voss, Uninvited
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Nell Voss, a sharp-tongued boat mechanic, starts helping with turtle patrols and warns Marguerite off her brother in no uncertain terms. Emotional beat: new alliance with barbed edges.

chapters.title: The Judge at the End of the Lane
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Callum visits Ezra Marsh, a retired judge living quietly outside town, who once tried to prosecute the Hollises and failed. Emotional beat: history surfaces — justice outside the law has a local lineage.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. After a committee win, Marguerite and Callum nearly kiss in the boathouse; she pulls away, terrified of being known by him of all people. Emotional beat: longing and self-protection at war.

chapters.title: The Letter That Cut
chapters.summary: Letters. Marguerite's pen pal writes something that feels devastatingly familiar; she begins to suspect who he is, and hates herself for hoping. Emotional bet: dread braided with hope.

chapters.title: Paper Trail
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Callum and Ezra quietly pull land records and find the Hollises bought the nesting beach through a shell company years ago. Emotional beat: the conspiracy takes shape; Callum chooses a side in secret.

chapters.title: Hatchling Night
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. During a mass hatching, Callum shows up unasked to help guard the beach, and they work side by side in the dark until dawn. Emotional beat: wordless intimacy — love arriving through shared labor.

chapters.title: The Kiss and the Lie
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Callum kisses her; she lets him, then lies that it was a mistake because she still believes he is the enemy of everything she's rebuilding. Emotional beat: heartbreak by choice.

chapters.title: Brother, Unmasked
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. Nell discovers Callum has been quietly funding the legal challenge against the marina permit and confronts him; old wounds between the Voss siblings finally bleed open. Emotional beat: grief turning toward forgiveness.

chapters.title: The Envelope
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The pen-pal program holds its winter reveal; Marguerite opens her envelope and reads Callum Voss's handwriting. Emotional beat: the floor drops out — every intimate letter rewrites itself in her memory.

chapters.title: What He Knew First
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Flashback chapter: Callum recognized Marguerite's voice in the first letter and kept writing anyway, hiding her past from the Hollises, who had been hunting her for testimony. Emotional beat: devotion revealed as deception's opposite.

chapters.title: Rage, Salt Water
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite confronts Callum on the dock; he tells her the Hollises destroyed her mentor's reputation and buried the evidence that could clear her — and that he can prove it. Emotional beat: fury and hope colliding.

chapters.title: Ezra's Box
chapters.summary: Marguerite and Ezra's POV. Ezra shows Marguerite his twenty-year file on the Hollises: bribed inspectors, a dead whistleblower, and a pattern that matches her own scandal exactly. Emotional beat: she was never the villain of her own story.

chapters.title: Terms of Trust
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Callum offers to hand the Hollises' documents to the state — if Marguerite will testify about what was done to her. She refuses; the law failed her once. Emotional beat: the theme sharpened — what is justice when the law won't hold?

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. The Hollis patriarch offers Callum the marina contract, a partnership, and his family's forgiveness — if he hands over Marguerite's name and the letters. Emotional beat: temptation priced in blood money.

chapters.title: Refusal at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Callum burns the bridge: he declines, leaks the shell-company deed to Nell, and knows his career in Port Alder is finished. Emotional beat: costly integrity — the price of survival made concrete.

chapters.title: The Town Decides
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The leaked deed ignites Port Alder; neighbors Marguerite once hid from now stand with her, and the town council schedules an emergency hearing. Emotional beat: belonging arriving unbidden.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Choice
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Callum urges her to stay anonymous and safe; she realizes safety has been another kind of hiding. She decides to testify under her real name. Emotional beat: the central choice made — the person over the career that was only ever a shelter.

chapters.title: The Hollis Counterstrike
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Hours before the hearing, the Hollises release Marguerite's old scandal file to the town, and her landlady's inn is vandalized. Emotional beat: darkest hour — the past weaponized, allies tested.

chapters.title: Standing Room Only
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. At the packed hearing, Marguerite takes the stand, tells the whole truth — the falsified data, the mentor, the fear — and the room listens. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into voice.

chapters.title: The Letters, Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. When her credibility is attacked, Callum publicly claims the letters as his own, reading one aloud to prove who Marguerite has been all along: honest. Emotional beat: public devotion, private vindication.

chapters.title: Ezra's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Ezra's POV. Ezra presents his decades of evidence; the state investigator in the audience opens a formal probe, and the marina permit is suspended pending review. Emotional beat: justice arriving sideways — outside the law, then finally inside it.

chapters.title: What It Cost
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Callum's firm fires him and blacklists him along the coast; Nell offers him a bunk and a job in her boatyard. Emotional beat: ruin and home in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Beach at Dawn
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite, raw after testifying, walks the nesting beach alone and admits to herself she loves him — and that love was never the risk; hiding was. Emotional beat: quiet certainty before the last leap.

chapters.title: The Last Letter
chapters.summary: Letters. Marguerite writes Callum one final letter, signed with her real name, and leaves it where only he will find it. Emotional beat: the anonymous device inverted — she chooses to be fully seen.

chapters.title: Port Alder Rising
chapters.summary: Marguerite and Callum's POV. Callum finds the letter at the boatyard; he comes to the beach at first light, and they meet as two people with no aliases left. Emotional beat: the kiss that costs nothing and means everything.

chapters.title: Nesting Grounds, Kept
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Weeks later: the beach is designated a protected reserve with Marguerite as its director, the Hollis probe widening, and Callum rebuilding dunes with his hands. Emotional beat: the career and the person, no longer at war.

chapters.title: Small Safe Steps, No Longer
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. At the town's summer festival, Marguerite speaks openly about her past, and the pen-pal program announces next winter's pairs. Emotional beat: belonging fully claimed — she is a Port Alder woman now, known and staying.

chapters.title: Epilogue: What the Turtles Know
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. One year on, Marguerite and Callum walk the beach at hatching dawn, a letter from the program in his pocket proposing they mentor the next pair together. Emotional beat: the long exhale — love, justice, and home all held at once.
